title: The Bell Witch: an invisible voice that haunted a Tennessee family
excerpt: Knocks, scratches and an invisible voice that argued with visitors terrorized a Tennessee farm between 1817 and 1821. What was behind the Bell Witch?
content:
Between 1817 and 1821, a farm near Adams (Tennessee) became the scene of blows, scratches and a voice that spoke and argued with visitors. The subject comes from a Milenio 3 special (Cadena SER), which presented it as a precursor to spiritualism. On foro3d.com we review the case of the Bell Witch.

What was told and what can be sustained today 👻

Tradition holds that the invisible entity's main targets were John Bell and his daughter Betsy, and that when he died in December 1820 the voice was blamed for his death. It is even said that Andrew Jackson visited the farm, although there is no evidence. The first extensive account was published in 1894, more than seventy years later, which makes it difficult to separate fact from legend. Skeptics point to pranks or family tensions as an explanation.

A witch with more biography than the Fox sisters 🕯️

The legend has inspired numerous films and is even credited with a presidential visit without evidence to support it. Seventy years between the events and the first extensive account leave room for memory to add details. Do you think there was something real in Adams or was it all a family joke that grew over the years? Tell us what you know.
